messages:
Samir Patel: publish job failed for py-ts SDK canary 2.1.1-beta -> npm rejected artifact, CI shows engines mismatch. pinging @jia for context

deploy-bot: [CI FAILED] publish-step (canary) 
```
npm ERR! code ENOTSUP
npm ERR! notsup Unsupported engine for @redwood/sdk@2.1.1-beta
npm ERR! notsup Not compatible with your version of node
```

Jia Chen: ah yeah, we added "engines": {"node": ">=18"} in the build to opt into new ESM bundling. Some users (and our CI runners) are still on 16. quick options: revert engines, publish a compat patch that relaxes it, or ship a tiny compat-shim that detects runtime and falls back.

Keon Park: prefer shim or revert? shim avoids churn for docs and changelog. but we mustn't change API surface. shim should be purely packaging-level (exports the same).

Maggie Rivera: idea: publish 2.1.1 with compat-shim, tag as `canary-shim`, do a staged rollout (canary -> next -> latest). simultaneously publish a short deprecation note for the legacy sync client that we plan to remove in 3.0.

Samir Patel: decision meeting quick: do compat-shim patch + staged rollout. If we detect any runtime errors we'll unpublish and revert. Jia can you prepare PR for the shim + updated package.json? Maggie can author release note. Keon, can you add publish-job flag for staggered dist-tag rollout?

Jia Chen: on it. shim sketch in case helpful: 
```
// packages/sdk/index.js
if (process.versions && parseInt(process.versions.node.split('.')[0], 10) < 18) {
  // load CJS-compatible entry that wraps ESM build
  module.exports = require('./cjs-compat.js');
} else {
  module.exports = require('./esm-entry.js');
}
```
This is purely an entrypoint switch; no surface API changes. Will open PR in 10m.

Keon Park: I'll add a `--staged-rollout` flag to the publish workflow and wire default 10% next, 48h window. Also add a fastfail step to revert dist-tag if error rate > 2% in the first hour.

release-bot: canary publish attempt succeeded: @redwood/sdk@2.1.1-canary-shim published to npm with dist-tag `canary-shim`. Digest: sha256:abc123

Samir Patel: nice. plan: observe for 2 hours, if healthy -> promote to `next` at 10% via traffic routing, then to `latest` after 48h. update changelog with migration snippet and deprecation note for sync client.

Maggie Rivera: draft release note: 
- "Fix: Restore compatibility for Node <18 via compat-shim (2.1.1). No API changes.
- Deprecation: legacy sync client marked deprecated, will be removed in 3.0; migrate to async client (example snippet included).
- Internal: staged rollout enabled for safer publish."
I'll push to GH release and docs and add migration snippet: 
```
// migrate: old sync -> async
const client = new RedwoodAsyncClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', prompt: '...' });
```

Jia Chen: PR opened: #4123 with package change + unit test for node version detection. build passes locally, CI queue shows canary publish done.

Keon Park: publish workflow updated in infra repo: new `staged-rollout` action, rollback hook added.

Samir Patel: monitoring hooks: @release-bot please surface error-rate alerts to #eng-releases and #prod-monitor if >1% token errors.

release-bot: staging rollout initiated: promoting `canary-shim` -> `next` with 10% routing. Monitoring watchers added.

Maggie Rivera: posting announcement draft to #product for sign-off, will include explicit migration callouts and a short timeline.

Samir Patel: if no regressions in 48h we promote to `latest` and close. If we see issues we will untag and unpublish 2.1.1 and fast-track a revert PR. Keep eyes on rollup errors and SDK telemetry. :eyes:

Keon Park: noted. I'll also add a temporary flag in SDK telemetry to tag events from canary-shim so we can filter.

Samir Patel: thanks all — closing this coordination thread, followups in PRs and the release checklist. If anyone spots a regression, post to #eng-releases and ping me directly. :thumbsup:
